rationale: "When will I get my card" fits card_arrival and card_delivery_estimate equally; the two label definitions overlap.
Text leads with "double charged"; predicted transaction_charged_twice fits at least as well as gold pending_card_payment.
Transfer direction is unstated: outgoing → pending_transfer, incoming → balance_not_updated. A human could not tell either.
"$1.00" matches the dataset's extra_charge_on_statement examples (the £1/$1 charge); "reversed" pulls toward reverted_card_payment?. The gold label is consistent with the dataset.
"How long does it take for transfers" is a clear transfer_timing cue; the phrase "reflect on my balance" pulls toward balance_not_updated.
"Paid for my top up twice … refund" reads as transaction_charged_twice or request_refund; gold top_up_reverted is a weak fit.
"Tried my card a bunch of times, never worked" fits card_not_working and declined_card_payment; overlapping definitions.
"What extra charges are there?" names no transaction type; gold transfer_fee_charged is not recoverable.
Ungrammatical; the intended action (cancel a transfer) cannot be recovered from the wording.
Weak fit for every code: a human can tell it is card_swallowed ("card wouldn't remove" while getting money), but it has no ATM/swallow keywords. Codebook gap: keyword-free paraphrase.
Garbled ("money I pushed … as being withdrawn"); what went wrong is unclear.
"Stole my wallet … block it" cues gold lost_or_stolen_card; "attempts to use the card" pulls toward cash_withdrawal_not_recognised.
Describes a declined credit-card purchase; prediction declined_card_payment looks correct and gold declined_transfer looks wrong.
In "withdraw some money … it disappeared in the machine", "it" can be the card (gold card_swallowed) or the money (prediction pending_cash_withdrawal). The referent is unclear.
A virtual card rejected at a merchant is genuinely both virtual_card_not_working and declined_card_payment; the definitions overlap, so it is not one misleading word.
Asks how to send an international transfer; gold transfer_into_account (receiving money) is a poor fit. The prediction exchange_rate is also wrong.
Nothing cues gold card_not_working; "unblock my card" is closer to pin_blocked. Gold is a loose fit.
"Am I allowed to use any card to make a payment?" asks which cards are supported; prediction supported_cards_and_currencies fits better than gold visa_or_mastercard.
"What's with not verifying my Id" can mean unable_to_verify or why_verify; overlapping labels.
"Someone stole my money" does not say the channel (direct debit, card, ATM).
"I had a transfer blocked" does not give the reason (beneficiary vs declined).
Asks about both countries and currencies; fiat_currency_support and country_support overlap.
"Transfer didn't get there" fits transfer_not_received_by_recipient and failed_transfer.
"How can I top-up my card?" fits topping_up_by_card at least as well as gold top_up_by_cash_or_cheque.
"Account does not accept cash deposits" asks about depositing cash (top_up_by_cash_or_cheque); gold is about a deposit already made that has not shown up.
"Can I exchange currencies?" matches exchange_via_app at least as well as gold fiat_currency_support.
"Base amount for cross-currency exchanges" sits between exchange_charge and exchange_rate; overlapping labels.
"Can't see the top-up amount I just added" fits pending_top_up better than gold topping_up_by_card.
A repeated failed transfer with no mention of the beneficiary; gold beneficiary_not_allowed is not recoverable.
"Exchange rate seems off on this transaction" does not say card payment or cash withdrawal.
